Hi Evelyn / Dev,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our infra team at ManufactureX is starting the internal design for the private deployment (VPC) and we need a concise headroom and network checklist from Redwood to firm up our procurement and rack/networking orders. Specifically we need: 

- Example throughput targets you recommend for a 24/7 serving pool targeting ~60k tokens/minute steady-state and 250 concurrent short-chat sessions (p50 latency target 150ms).
- Guidance on NICs / MTU / RDMA vs TCP, and whether jumbo frames are required for your KV cache syncs.
- A simple runbook for scale-up/down and a short canary plan for rolling in new nodes.

Can you send a short package we can hand to our networking vendor? Also indicate any lead times on provisioning if we want a staged launch (pilot -> ramp -> steady).

Appreciate it — Matt

Subject: Re: Private GPU pool - initial headroom request and network checklist

Matt / team — attaching the model and initial checklist. Key takeaways up-front:

Attachment: redwood_gpub_headroom_calc.xlsx (sheet summary)
- Baseline assumptions: average request = 240 tokens, 60k tokens/min steady => ~250 requests/min.
- GPU profile used: A100 80GB (single-worker tight-KV), baseline perf = 1,800 tokens/sec per GPU for mixed prompt lengths.
- Steady-state sizing: 8 GPUs gives ~8640 tokens/sec => 518,400 tokens/min nominal. Given burst patterns and cache misses, we recommend a minimum of 10 GPUs for the pilot (headroom ~22%) and 14 GPUs for initial ramp (headroom ~75%).
- Canary pool: reserve 2 GPUs outside production pool for canary/rollouts.

Network checklist (high level) — see network-checklist-vpc.pdf attached
- NICs: 2x 25GbE bonded (or 2x 50GbE). For cluster RDMA use Mellanox/NVIDIA ConnectX-6.
- MTU: set to 9000 (jumbo frames) across host and switch for KV syncs and large model shards. Confirm all intermediate switches and firewalls support 9k.
- RDMA: recommended for <1ms intra-rack latency for KV-cache heavy workloads, but TCP/HTTP is acceptable for cross-rack with properly sized NICs.
- Switch config: L2 jumbo frames, disable flow-control at host level if using RDMA, ensure PFC settings are consistent with vendor docs.
- Routing: BGP with eBGP sessions for cross-AZ failover; prefer static routes within VPC for low jitter.
- Firewall/NAT: allow outbound TLS to Redwood control plane (list of IPs in PDF) and open high ports for node heartbeats as noted.

Operational runbook (summary) — runbook-private-pool.md attached
- Scale up: add GPU node -> wait for health checks -> join LB -> warm cache (preload top N prompts) -> shift traffic in 5% increments over 10m.
- Scale down: drain -> wait 30m for KV sync -> remove and power-off. Automatic policy: scale when 95th percentile token latency > target for 2 consecutive 5m windows.
- Failure cases: if KV sync fails, fall back to read-only model variant and alert on-call.

Lead-times and staging
- Pilot (10 GPUs) procurement: 4–6 weeks to order and rack, or 2–3 weeks if you have available stock.
- Ramp to 14 GPUs: add in 2–3 week increments depending on vendor delivery.
- If you want encapsulated Dedicated (Redwood-managed) we can provide temporary Hosted routing to avoid immediate procurement.

Open questions for ManufactureX:
1) Do you have a preferred NIC vendor or are you tied to existing switch inventory?
2) Can your networking team confirm jumbo-frames are possible across the intended data path?
3) Any regulatory constraints requiring air-gapped or restricted egress?

I'll hand off the XLS, PDF checklist, and a Markdown runbook in a shared drive link after this thread.

— Dev

Thanks Dev — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick clarifications before we hand to our procurement team: 

- The A100 80GB perf number (1,800 tokens/sec): is that for a single model variant (e.g., 70B) or conservative across several model sizes? We're planning to run a 13B distilled model primarily with occasional 70B spikes.
- For the canary plan, any advice on traffic split (we usually do 5-10% canary). Is a 5% steady split enough given your warm-cache description?
- Regarding jumbo frames: our switches may not support 9k end-to-end for cross-rack; we can enable it intra-rack. How much hit on latency/cost if RDMA only intra-rack and TCP across racks?

Also please send the shared drive link and the runbook PDF we can attach to the vendor ticket.

Matt
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Jenkins <matthew.jenkins@manufacturex.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private GPU pool - initial headroom request and network checklist

Matt — quick answers and next steps: 

- The perf number is conservative for mixed-size workloads; for a primarily 13B run (with occasional 70B) you can expect ~+20–30% throughput per GPU vs the 1,800 value. We'll annotate the XLS with a 13B column.
- Canary split: 5% is fine for functional checks but for load behavior and warm-cache churn we recommend a staged approach: 5% -> 15% -> 50% (each step 20–30m with traffic observation). We included the canary/rollout script in runbook-private-pool.md.
- Jumbo frames intra-rack only: that is an acceptable compromise. Expect ~8–12% higher CPU/network processing cost for cross-rack TCP compared to full RDMA with jumbo frames; latency variance will be slightly higher (p95 delta ~10–30ms depending on rack cross-traffic). We'll call this out in the checklist so procurement can prioritize intra-rack 9k support if full end-to-end isn't possible.

Shared files (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_headroom
Attachments included in this thread: redwood_gpub_headroom_calc.xlsx, network-checklist-vpc.pdf, runbook-private-pool.md

If those look good, can we schedule a 45-minute dry-run session with your networking and SRE leads the week of Oct 19? Laura, Hiro and I can join.

— Evelyn
